title: And the Two Shall Be One Flesh
attribution_note: St Luke of Simferopol (Voino-Yasenetsky, 1877–1961). His I budut dvoe odna plot, on the relationship of husband and wife, from the collection O seme i vospitanii detei. Translated here fresh from the Russian with credit and a link to the source, not offered as public domain. Source: https://azbyka.ru/otechnik/Luka_Vojno-Jasenetskij/o-seme-i-vospitanii-detej/

pairs.en:
And the two shall be one flesh.
On the relationship between husband and wife in marriage, holy apostle Paul spoke great words: "Wives, submit to your husbands as to the Lord, because the husband is head of the wife, as Christ also is Head of the Church. But as the Church submits to Christ, so also wives to their husbands in everything. Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved the Church and gave Himself for it. So husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself. For no one ever hated his own flesh, but feeds and warms it, as the Lord does the Church, because we are members of His body, of His flesh and of His bones. Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall be one flesh. This mystery is great; I speak in relation to Christ and to the Church. So let each one of you love his wife as himself; and let the wife fear her husband" [Eph. 5:22–25, 28–32].
How the apostle Paul exalts the marriage union! Can there be a higher likeness of marriage than its likeness to the union of Christ and the Church? This raises the holiness of the marriage bond between man and woman to an unreachable height. The Lord heads the Church as the head crowns our body. In it lies the brain, the most important of all our body's organs. From Christ, as from a root, all members of the Church are fed with holy divine sap. In Him is our life, and so the Church is holy. And in marriage, from the husband as from the head, flows everything best, everything needed for the family to thrive.

The kinds of love are many: there is the love of husband for wife, of wife for husband, the love of parents for children, the love of children for parents. There is also a higher form of love — love for all people, for in every person we must see the image of God. And there is the most perfect degree of love, the highest and the holiest — love for God.
In every undertaking we must climb step by step from the simple to the higher. So let marriage serve us as a school of love. Married love is easy. It is sustained by the strong unceasing pull of one flesh toward another. It is strengthened by the unbreakable bodily bond. The bodies of man and woman complete each other. Through this a new person is conceived into the world. But physical love must not be the aim of marriage. In it we must learn higher love: a man must love his wife not for her flesh but for her pure soul and good heart. A wife has what a husband lacks; she completes him spiritually, and he her. So in the life of husband and wife those qualities of spirit, mind, and heart that belong to man alone and to woman alone must show themselves with tremendous force.
In marriage a man finds a great filling-up of his being, the treasures of his spirit from the treasures of his wife's soul. The roughness of a man's heart is made whole by the tenderness and purity of his wife's heart, for a woman's heart is far finer, far more ready for spiritual love.

And a wife must remember: God gave man at first greater bodily strength than hers. In most cases His powers of mind far surpass a woman's. In her life with her husband she must make up for her lack of strength with his knowledge, with his strong will. Man and woman must become in marriage one body and one soul. Something higher must be born of their union, joining all the good and great that is in each of them. Is this not enrichment?! Is this not the grace of God?! Is not this the whole mystery of marriage, the deepest meaning of the marriage bond?
"Wives, submit to your husbands as to the Lord, because the husband is head of the wife." This means a wife must be in a loving, gentle, free submission to her husband. When we speak of submission, at once proud people — and proud women above all — blaze up with indignation. They will not hear even of obedience in love; they demand full equality between husband and wife.
And in our country, so unlike all other countries, with its own laws and customs, a woman is set in every way on a level with a man. She has been given all rights: political, civil, family. Is it a good thing that woman has won full freedom? Blessed is woman's full freedom in the spiritual sense, but must there not be some limits to that freedom? For woman even in her bodily makeup is different from man. The features of a woman's anatomy and physiology shape her spiritual life in many ways. God, who created the wife after the husband, made her as his helper. A woman, in keeping with the deepest features of her bodily makeup, has a great calling that a man does not have — bearing children and, therefore, raising them. For you cannot bear a child and cast it aside. On parents, and above all on the mother, lies the holiest duty — to raise the child and give it upbringing. This duty is a woman's heaviest burden.

sections.heading: Children, the family, and the state

pairs.en:
Everything great, eternal, holy must always be put first. So it is necessary that in a woman's life this most important task take the first place. A woman is answerable for the raising of children before the state and before society. More than that, she cannot and must not refuse this duty, for she would commit a grave sin. Let her pursue science and all difficult work alongside men, but at the same time never forget her primary calling.
Unfortunately, full equality of women with men in every field of physical and mental labour has had a result. The raising of children in the family is in a woeful state. The school cannot replace the far more important family upbringing.
Who raises the children in such families? Both father and mother hold important public posts. They are at work from morning till night, with neither the time nor the strength nor the chance to look after the children. In the great majority of cases — no one. It is a good thing when an old kind nanny brings up the children in the house. But not every family has a pious old woman. A family with no one to raise the children does not form a single unbroken spiritual whole. From this there can be no well-being either in society or in the state. For a state is strong when it is made up of strong, morally healthy families. As the human body, made up of separate cells, only lives its full life when all the cells of the organism function normally, so too society, made up of many separate families. If some of the cells are struck by any disease, this will inevitably show in the whole organism.
A family is not well when a woman takes on the role of a man, refusing those holy family duties for which God Himself designed her. If marriage is so great that the holy apostle likens it to the union of Christ Himself and the Church, must it not be hallowed by the grace of God, by the blessing of the Church? Must not the greatest of human acts — the marriage union of husband and wife — have at its foundation full obedience to God? People who give themselves in full obedience to God feel the need for this. They want every step, every deed hallowed by the blessing of the Church, by prayer, by the Sacrament.

Church marriage is not obligatory for anyone now, and many families live in civil registration. But you, Christians, taking the most important step in your life as you enter marriage — do you not need the blessing of the Church? Must not your union be hallowed by the Sacrament of Crowning?
In deep antiquity the people of Israel regarded marriage with deep reverence, and not at all as they do now. People could not imagine a marriage not hallowed by prayer. When our great forefather Abraham wanted to find a worthy wife for his only son Isaac, he called his favourite servant. He sent him to that far country from which he himself had come out at God's command. He told him to find there among his kindred a wife for his son (see Gen. 24). He asked God to send his Angel along. He asked for God's protection, entrusting to that protection the great matter of his son's marriage union. The good servant came to Mesopotamia, where Abraham's kin lived. He stopped at a well to water his camels. He turned to God with a wonderful prayer: "Lord, God of my master Abraham! Send her today to meet me and show kindness to my master Abraham. Behold, I stand at the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water; and the maiden to whom I say, 'Tip your pitcher, let me drink,' and who says to me, 'Drink, and I will water your camels also' — she is the one whom You have appointed for Your servant Isaac; and by this I shall know that You show kindness to my master Abraham" [Gen. 24:12–14].
And before he had finished this prayer, Rebecca came to the well and did all that he had asked of God. He took this as a sign that she was the God-chosen bride for Isaac. And she invited him to the house of her father Bethuel and her brother Laban. And there he told them why he had come, who had sent him, that God had heard his prayer, and he understood that Rebecca must be Isaac's wife. And Bethuel and Laban answered: "The matter comes from the Lord; we cannot speak to you either bad or good. Behold, Rebecca is before you; take her and go; let her be a wife to your master's son, as the Lord has said" [Gen. 24:50–51]. That is how marriage was made and hallowed in ancient times.
Remembering this, let us set side by side the reverence and obedience to God with which the Israelites approached marriage against today's civil registration. What comes of those marriages that are strangers to God's blessing?

How often now the motive for marriage is nothing but lust, the fleshly pull of a man toward a woman, without any moral duty, without any deep understanding of what marriage means. Yet the Lord by His presence hallowed marriage at Cana in Galilee (see John 2:1–11). And if He Himself saw fit to do so, must not all of us hallow our marriage union with the great Sacrament of Crowning?
Once the Pharisees came to the Lord and asked "whether it is lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause?" He answered them: "Have you not read that He who made them at the beginning made them male and female?" And He said: "Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh, so that they are no longer two but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined, let not man separate" [Matt. 19:3–6]. That is what the marriage union is in the eyes of the Lord. He commands us not to divorce, except only when marital faithfulness has been broken.
And how many wretched adulterers there are among us now. How many pitiless men there have become, who to satisfy their lust with another unclean woman abandon their wives with children to the mercy of fate.

sections.heading: You will give God a terrible answer

pairs.en:
And you, wretched adulterers, you will give God a terrible answer. You will answer for the blood with which your wife's heart was drenched — the wife you abandoned for an adulteress. God Himself joined you to your wives. Innocent, good girls gave you everything precious they had. They gave you their virginity, the purity of body and heart, their reaching toward love — not only family love but higher love, Divine Love.
They waited and they wait for you to be their guardians, to help them walk the path of holiness, of chastity. With them you were to walk all your life along the hard stony road that leads to the Kingdom of God. But you have gone into the house of a harlot. Have you never heard the words of apostle Paul: "Let marriage be held in honour by all, and let the marriage bed be undefiled; but God will judge the fornicators and adulterers" [Heb. 13:4]?
How then dare you trample underfoot the purity of a woman's heart!? What are you doing, forgetting that the Lord God made you one flesh with your wife!? What are you doing, you whom God has set at the head of the family!? Can you not see what horror happens to your children when you abandon your wives? Can you not see the children's eyes cast darkly to the ground? Can you not see the suffering of a child's heart: "How can it be that my father has left my mother!?" And they weep and wail. Then they grow bitter. Then, having seen such a bad example in their father, they turn their eyes to other bad examples. They go out into the street, to the markets. There they draw from the well of filth, of evil, of godlessness. And they perish with eternal death.
Is the coming Judgment not terrifying to you!? Now it may not seem terrifying, because you cannot picture it in all its force. But when you stand before it, you will tremble with your whole heart. And you will curse the unclean woman with whom you defiled for the sake of lust the marriage bed prepared for you by God. You who are perishing — if you will not listen to my words, then perhaps the words of Holy Scripture will bring you to your senses. The words of the Lord Jesus Christ Himself: "What God has joined, let not man separate!" — fear the Judgment of Christ! Let these words hold you back from falling into the abyss.

sections.heading: Build your marriage blessed by God

pairs.en: Recognise the duty laid upon you in the marriage union — first before God, then before society and the state. Remember the words about the importance of marriage and build it so that it is a union blessed by God Himself, to whom be glory and dominion forever and ever! Amen.
